description: Systematic quant funds experienced a correlated unwind as overlapping factor portfolios deleveraged simultaneously. Momentum and statistical arbitrage strategies lost 10-15% in a single week as crowded positions reversed. The event was self-reinforcing: initial selling forced further liquidation. First documented case of crowding-driven factor crash.

Lehman Brothers collapse triggered systemic deleveraging. Quality (low-leverage, stable-earnings) stocks initially sold off as forced liquidations were indiscriminate. Low-vol factor also suffered as correlations spiked to 1. Factor diversification broke down completely. The crisis demonstrated that factor risk premia can vanish during liquidity crises.

Deep value positions continued to deteriorate as the financial system remained impaired. Value investors who bought the 2008 dip faced continued drawdowns as bank and industrial stocks hit new lows. The 'value trap' dynamic: cheap stocks got cheaper. Quality and low-vol significantly outperformed during this sub-period.

Eurozone sovereign debt crisis escalated with Greek exit fears (Grexit). Risk-off rotation out of high-beta momentum names into defensive low-vol. Momentum factor reversed sharply as high-flying tech and cyclical names sold off. VIX spiked from 15 to 27. Classic momentum crash driven by macro risk-off rather than factor-specific crowding.

The XIV (inverse VIX ETF) collapse triggered a short-vol unwind. Low-volatility equity strategies suffered as stocks that had been 'volatility-laundered' corrected sharply. The crowding in short-vol and low-vol strategies amplified the selloff. VIX spiked from 15 to 50 intraday on Feb 5. Low-vol factor lost over 5% in 5 days, reversing 2 years of alpha.

COVID-19 pandemic triggered one of the fastest bear markets in history. Quality factor (stable earnings, low leverage) initially outperformed but was subsequently sold in forced liquidations. Low-vol factor also suffered dramatically as realized volatility spiked. The crash exposed the limits of defensive factor positioning against systemic liquidity crises.

Rotation from growth/momentum into value/cyclical stocks as vaccine optimism rose and rates began moving higher. High-momentum tech names that had surged in the WFH trade reversed sharply. Classic momentum crash: the factor had become extremely crowded after a 6-month chase of COVID winners. MTUM ETF underperformed the market by over 8% in 2 weeks.

Fed pivot toward rate hikes triggered a repricing of long-duration assets. Quality/growth stocks (high P/E, high earnings quality) sold off sharply as discount rates rose. The quality factor, which had become crowded with long-duration tech names, underperformed significantly. This event marked the beginning of the 2022 factor regime shift from growth to value.
